subject: Excessive memory use for regression model

messages.author: d42c7062482960a4
messages.subject: Excessive memory use for regression model
parts:
I'm trying to run a fairly complex linear regression model with many nested random intercepts and slopes and an autocorrelation term and a PC prior. I run this on different subsets of my data, which have between several 100 and 10.000 species (random effects) each, and each takes at least a day to run. But so far each model has crashed after at least 1 day of running, most with a Bus error, or an out or memory warning, and some don't specify.
I ran the smallest subset (few 100 species)  on an HPC with 1 TB of memory (after several tries with less memory), which still doesn't seem to be enough. The problem seems to arise in the integration phase (as far as I understand the inner working of INLA).

What can I do to make memory use more efficient? Since each test run for the smallest subset takes me > 36h, it's a rather time and energy consuming endeavor. The larger model I tried had a time-out after 6 days.

Another problem I have is with parallelization, which doesn't seem to work with the num.threads = 4 argument (it still runs on one core only), but I suspect this will also not solve my memory usage in the integration phase.


Model specification:

sd.res <- 3 * sd(log10(dat$Number+1), na.rm = T)
prior.prec <- list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(sd.res, 0.01))) #1% prob bigger than 1


model <- inla( log10(Number+1) ~  cYear  ,                                    # number of individuals explained by Year
            +f(Period_4INLA,model='iid', hyper = prior.prec)+ # random intercepts
                         f(Plot_ID_4INLA,model='iid', hyper = prior.prec )+
                         f(Location_4INLA,model='iid', hyper = prior.prec)+
                         f(Datasource_ID_4INLA,model='iid', hyper = prior.prec)+
                         f(Plot_ID_4INLAs,iYear,model='iid', hyper = prior.prec)+  # random slopes
                         f(Location_4INLAs,iYear,model='iid', hyper = prior.prec)+
                         f(Datasource_ID_4INLAs,iYear,model='iid', hyper = prior.prec)+
                         f(iYear, model='ou', replicate=as.numeric(Plot_ID_4INLA),  # AR term
                                        hyper = list(theta1 = list(prior='pc.prec', param=c(0.5, 0.01)))),
                             family  = gaussian,
              control.compute = list(    
                config = TRUE,
                dic=TRUE,
                waic=TRUE,
                cpo = TRUE),
              control.inla = list( tolerance =  1e-08),
               control.predictor = list(link = 1) , verbose = T,
              quantiles=c(0.001, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 0.95, 0.975, 0.99, 0.999)  ,    
                num.threads = 1, blas.num.threads = 1,
                data=dat)

Any help is appreciated

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Excessive memory use for regression model
parts:
can you make sure you have this version

This is INLA_22.12.16 built 2022-12-23 13:24:10 UTC.

(you'll need R-4.2)

if that does not work, can you share code/data so I can rerun a case
here?

I see you force num.threads=1, this will reduce the MEM requirements but
make it slower

If you're running on Windows, then running this withing WSL and then use
PARDISO will help as well

Let me know

Best
H

you can set

control.inla=list(int.strategy="eb")

to avoid the issue about the integration phase. yes, at that point the
mem requirement peaks

inla.binary.install()

will install new binaries as the default build is Ubuntu-2004, usually

inla.pardiso()

you have to register your University username and email to get the key

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Excessive memory use for regression model
parts:
Hi Harvard
I solved the problem by changing the autoregression parameter. It now doesn't calculate AR on each (sometimes sparse) species in every plot, but over all species in a plot. This has shrunk memory needs to ~ 100gb.
I also noticed that some kind of parallelization must still occur, since the models run much faster with threads = 4. I hypothesise that the estimations for each random effect are parallelized, but don't require much memory per CPU. Only when the integration is done, does it require the full 200gb of any CPU.

My institute is not very fast with new software on the HPC, so they have earliest started working on this this week.

In any case, thanks for your help.

Roel

On Saturday, December 31, 2022 at 12:00:02 PM UTC+1 he...@r-inla.org wrote:
with the HPC, inform them that

inla.binary.install()

will install new binaries as the default build is Ubuntu-2004, usually
the CentOS7 is the good option.

PARDISO: this you have to enable on a user-basis, see

inla.pardiso()

you have to register your University username and email to get the key
